original_question: For σ ∈ Sn and τ ∈ Sm, where n ⩽ m, let dflex n(σ, τ) = (1/n) · (|{x ∈ {1,..., n} | σ(x) ̸= τ (x)}| + (m − n)). An almost-homomorphism {fn } is said to be flexibly close to a homomorphism if there is a sequence of group homomorphisms ρn: G → Smn with n ⩽ mn such that dflex n(ρn(g), fn(g)) → 0 as n → ∞ for all g ∈ G. The group G is said to be flexibly permutation stable if every almost-homomorphism of G is flexibly close to a homomorphism. Is SLn(Z) flexibly permutation-stable?
target_in_paper: The draft is trying to capture the flexible-permutation-stability question introduced by Becker–Lubotzky in Section 4.4 (“A flexible variant of P-stability”), sharpened by Ioana’s official formulation of flexible P-stability and his remark that it is open whether groups with property (τ) can be flexibly P-stable. Specialized to the arithmetic example from Becker–Lubotzky’s Theorem 1.3, this becomes the question for SL_r(Z).
correct_elements: The draft correctly identifies the right stability notion as the flexible variant of permutation/P-stability, correctly captures the idea of allowing extra points before correcting an almost action, and reproduces Becker–Lubotzky’s cross-size defect metric d_flex from Section 4.4. It also picks a paper-faithful higher-rank arithmetic test case, namely SL_n(Z), which is central in Becker–Lubotzky’s discussion.
missing_details: The paper-faithful modern formulation uses asymptotic homomorphisms σ_k: G → Sym(X_k) on finite sets X_k; your draft calls {f_n} an almost-homomorphism but does not state the asymptotic homomorphism condition d_H(σ_k(gh), σ_k(g)σ_k(h)) → 0 for all g,h ∈ G.
Your notation overloads n: it appears both in SL_n(Z) and in S_n. These should be separated, e.g. use r for the matrix rank and k for the approximation index.
To match the higher-rank arithmetic case treated around Theorem 1.3, the rank should be fixed with r ≥ 3; r = 2 is a qualitatively different case and is not the intended Property-(T)/(τ) example.
The official flexible-P-stability definition needs finite supersets X_k ⊂ Y_k together with genuine homomorphisms τ_k: G → Sym(Y_k).
The size control |Y_k|/|X_k| → 1 is essential for flexible P-stability; without it one gets the weaker 'very flexible' notion.

The comparison between σ_k(g) and τ_k(g) should be stated using the normalized Hamming metric on the same set, namely d_H(σ_k(g), τ_k(g)|_{X_k}), unless one explicitly chooses the Becker–Lubotzky presentation-based d_flex framework.

If one insists on the Becker–Lubotzky Section 4.4 formulation, one must first fix a finite generating set S and quotient map π: F_S → G, and define a P-stability challenge by requiring relator-defect d_H(f_k(w), id) → 0 for every w ∈ ker π.
The quantifiers should be explicit: the approximation condition is for every g,h ∈ G, and the correction condition is for every g ∈ G.
The draft does not specify whether it is asking for flexible P-stability or very flexible P-stability; in the relevant literature these are distinct notions unless additional hypotheses are invoked.
The paper-level intent is a single-group question for a fixed group G, so the refined question should ask about a fixed SL_r(Z), not leave the rank implicit.
refined_question: Fix an integer r ≥ 3. Is the group SL_r(Z) flexibly P-stable in permutations? Equivalently, if d_H denotes the normalized Hamming metric on permutations of a finite set, does every asymptotic homomorphism σ_k: SL_r(Z) → Sym(X_k) on finite sets X_k—meaning that d_H(σ_k(gh), σ_k(g)σ_k(h)) → 0 for every g,h ∈ SL_r(Z)—admit finite supersets X_k ⊂ Y_k with |Y_k|/|X_k| → 1 and genuine homomorphisms τ_k: SL_r(Z) → Sym(Y_k) such that d_H(σ_k(g), τ_k(g)|_{X_k}) → 0 for every g ∈ SL_r(Z)?
justification: Your draft mixes two nearby formulations from the literature: Becker–Lubotzky’s Section 4.4 presentation-based d_flex definition, and the later full-group asymptotic-homomorphism formulation used by Ioana. The nearest official open formulation is Ioana’s remark that it is unknown whether groups with property (τ) can be flexibly P-stable; the natural arithmetic specialization, staying close to Becker–Lubotzky’s surrounding discussion, is to ask this for a fixed higher-rank group SL_r(Z), r ≥ 3, especially since Becker–Lubotzky had just proved that SL_n(Z), n ≥ 3, is not P-stable in the strict sense. The refined question therefore keeps your target group and stability notion, but replaces the incomplete 'almost-homomorphism' language by the paper-standard asymptotic-homomorphism quantifiers and the essential size condition |Y_k|/|X_k| → 1.
